quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines are doubled in work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycles may cross here.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn drivers about road hazards. This sign tells drivers to watch for bicycles crossing the road.

questions.question: Look ahead of your motorcycle for ______ seconds.
questions.correctAnswerText: 20 seconds
questions.explanation: Look 20 seconds ahead of your motorcycle on the road. This gives you time to see dangers and react before you reach them.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes involve:

options.text: Riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a new motorcycle. Most motorcycle crashes happen with riders who have less than six months of experience on that bike.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Keep riding—it will stop on its own.
Slow down by closing the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by closing the throttle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars tight, close the throttle to slow down, lean forward, and pull off the road safely. Then fix the problem causing the wobble.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle turns:
questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Extra weight means the motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn.

questions.question: In Wisconsin, who must wear a helmet?

options.text: Riders with a license for less than five years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders under age 18.
questions.explanation: Wisconsin law requires helmets for riders under 18 and riders with instruction permits. All riders and passengers should wear helmets for safety.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has a sharp right turn followed by a sharp left turn.

questions.question: Braking while turning is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
Harder than braking on a straight road.
Safe if you use only the front brake.
Safe if you use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking while turning is more difficult than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must know the right technique and be very careful.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see better, keeps you out of blind spots, avoids wind blasts and road hazards, and gives you an escape route. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders be placed?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Staggered riding is usually best. But when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a highway, riders should switch to single-file.

questions.question: When it starts raining, it is best to:

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, avoid the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track often works best, but it depends on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: Impairment from drinking alcohol occurs:

options.text: Once you reach the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Well below the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Never ride a motorcycle after drinking any amount of alcohol. Impairment starts well below the legal limit.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
The driver usually cannot see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in a position where the car driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This usually means riding in the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No parking.
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers rules they must follow. This sign means you cannot park here.

questions.question: The formation you should take when riding in a group:
questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best. Switch to single-file when taking a curve, making a turn, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign shows an arrow pointing right with a line through it. It means you cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen with riders who have little experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Place less experienced riders toward the front, just behind the leader. This way, more experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers rules they must follow. This sign tells you to stay to the right to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should:

options.text: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Only wear hearing protection on long rides.
Not wear hearing protection because it blocks horns and sirens.
Not need hearing protection if wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage, even with a full-face helmet. Earplugs protect your hearing while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through turns to see where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: This sign means you are approaching a railroad crossing with no signal. You should:

options.text: Keep going at the same speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At this crossing, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains and be ready to stop if one is near. Never try to outrun a train.

questions.question: This sign is a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black lettering or symbols. They warn drivers about hazards or special situations ahead.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Look through every turn by turning only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: To work well, a face shield should NOT:
questions.correctAnswerText: Be airtight.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should have no scratches, let you see to the sides clearly, fasten securely, and let air pass through. An airtight shield causes fogging, making it hard to see.

questions.question: If you brake while turning:

options.text: It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more traction as you lean.
You may have less traction as you lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but it takes care. When the motorcycle leans, some tire grip goes to the turn. Less grip is left for braking.

questions.question: A helmet gives the most protection if it is all of the following, EXCEPT:
questions.correctAnswerText: Loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: A helmet protects best when it meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly all around, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: All traffic must go straight ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows an intersection ahead. A road joins from the right.

questions.question: Shifting gears while turning:

options.text: Should only be done if it is smooth.
Is better than shifting before the turn.
Is the best way to control speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it is smooth.
questions.explanation: It is best to shift before you turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change can cause a skid.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on a good surface, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If you accidentally lock the rear brake on a good surface, you can keep it locked until you stop. You should still be able to steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: What should you do before every ride?

options.text: Make sure the clutch feels loose and free.
Make sure both brakes can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure both brakes can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Check each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and holds the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, use both brakes when slowing or stopping, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these surfaces are more slippery.

questions.question: If you are in traffic and a small animal enters your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Do whatever you can, including swerving into other lanes, to avoid the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Avoid hitting an animal if you can do so safely. In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting a larger vehicle.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction opposite of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward. Press the opposite handgrip to return to your original direction once you are clear of the hazard.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal after you finish a turn or lane change. Leaving your signal on can confuse other drivers.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at a minimum?
questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Regular motorcycle inspections before riding are important for safety. Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week.

questions.question: What do convex mirrors do?

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. They also make objects look farther away than they really are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has convex mirrors.

questions.question: A sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars is usually caused by what?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
The front wheel not being tightened properly to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
questions.explanation: Front wheel and handlebar shaking is usually caused by improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: As your weight moves forward while braking, what can you do?

options.text: Reduce pressure on the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: As your weight shifts forward while braking, the front wheel has more traction. This means you can apply the front brake harder.
